e.etymology: A phonetic spelling of Gianna, the Italian short form of Giovanna, which is the feminine of John, from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious.
The Spanish word for dove, from Latin palumbus. As a name it honors the Virgen de la Paloma, a title of Mary venerated in Madrid, and the dove as a sign of peace and the Holy Spirit.
namesakes: Paloma Picasso (jewelry designer, daughter of Pablo Picasso)

assoc.t: Paloma, tequila and grapefruit soda cocktail

e.etymology: From Greek barbaros, foreign, through the Latin name of Saint Barbara, an early martyr said to have been locked in a tower. It was a top-ten American girls' name from 1927 to 1958.
namesakes: Barbara Walters (television journalist)
Barbara Bush (First Lady)
Barbara Eden (star of I Dream of Jeannie)

e.etymology: The Spanish and Italian feminine of Luis and Luigi, forms of Louis, from the Frankish Hludwig, famous in battle. It rose in the US after Luisa, the strong sister in Disney's Encanto (2021).

assoc.t: Luisa Madrigal, the super-strong sister in Disney's Encanto

e.etymology: From Greek Thaddaios, the New Testament form of the Aramaic name Thaddai, borne by one of the twelve apostles. Its meaning is uncertain; it is often explained as heart.
namesakes: Thaddeus Stevens (antislavery congressman of the Civil War era)
Thaddeus Ross (general in the Marvel films)

e.etymology: A spelling of Cara, taken from Italian cara, dear or beloved, or Irish cara, friend. Neither word was a traditional given name; Cara and Kara arose in the English-speaking world in the 20th century.

assoc.t: Supergirl, whose real name is Kara Zor-El

e.etymology: A pet form of Madeline, the English form of Magdalene, woman from Magdala, and of Madison. It is increasingly given as a full name.
namesakes: Maddie Ziegler (dancer from Dance Moms and Sia's music videos)

e.etymology: A respelling of Austin, the medieval English short form of Augustine, from Latin augustus, venerable or majestic. The -yn spelling is used mostly for girls.
A Swedish pet form of Anna, from Hebrew Hannah, grace, first recorded in Sweden in 1521 and modeled on the Low German Anneke. Americans know it from golfer Annika Sörenstam.
namesakes: Annika Sörenstam (Hall of Fame golfer)

assoc.t: Annika Sörenstam, Hall of Fame golfer

e.etymology: The Russian form of Zoe, from Greek zoe, life. It is also widely used in India and Pakistan.
A respelling of the Hawaiian Leilani, from lei, a flower garland, and lani, sky or heaven. The spelling leans on Layla.
A spelling of Casey, an Irish surname from Ó Cathasaigh, descendant of Cathasach, a byname meaning vigilant. In America the name also spread through the folk hero engineer Casey Jones.
namesakes: Kasey Kahne (NASCAR driver)

e.meaning: healthy second son, among other readings
e.etymology: A Japanese name whose meaning depends on the characters chosen: ken can be healthy, wise or modest, and ji often marks a second son or means to govern.

e.meaning: triumph or to open (Vietnamese); also a spelling of Kai
e.etymology: In Vietnamese, Khai is a male name of Chinese origin, written with characters such as khải, triumph, or khai, to open. In the US it is also used as a spelling of Kai, Hawaiian for sea.
An English place name and surname from Old English lang, long or tall, and stan, stone. As a first name it honors the Harlem Renaissance poet Langston Hughes.
namesakes: Langston Hughes (Harlem Renaissance poet)

e.etymology: The Spanish form of William, through Old French Guillaume from the Frankish Willahelm: wil, will or desire, and helm, helmet or protection.
namesakes: Guillermo del Toro (director of Pan's Labyrinth and The Shape of Water)
Guillermo Rodriguez (sidekick on Jimmy Kimmel Live)

e.etymology: From Arabic mustafa, the chosen one, an epithet of the Prophet Muhammad. It is especially common in Turkey, where it was the given name of Atatürk.
namesakes: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk (founder of modern Turkey)

e.etymology: A pet form of Ruth, from a Hebrew name probably meaning friend or companion. Ruth is the loyal daughter-in-law whose story fills the Old Testament book of Ruth.
The name of the North African country, through Latin from Greek Aigyptos, which goes back to an ancient Egyptian name for the city of Memphis. Alicia Keys gave the name to her son in 2010.

assoc.t: Egypt, country of the Nile and the pyramids

e.etymology: A combination of Lee and Anna, or Leanne with an -a ending. Some treat it as a spelling of Liana.
A respelling of Bailey, an English surname for a bailiff or steward, from Old French bailli.
namesakes: Bailee Madison (actress in Bridge to Terabithia)

e.etymology: From Hebrew Qetsiah, cassia, a fragrant bark related to cinnamon. Keziah was the second of the three daughters born to Job after his trials.
A spelling of Derek, which came into English in the Middle Ages from a Low German form of Theodoric, ruler of the people, and was revived in the 19th century.
A spelling of Liliana that puts Lily up front, and the usual English rendering of the Bulgarian form. All go back to Lillian and the lily, Latin lilium.
Used as a spelling of Reina, Spanish for queen, and of Rayna. Raina is also a Bulgarian name, and it looks like Rain with an -a ending. No single origin accounts for American use.
namesakes: Raina Telgemeier (graphic novelist, author of Smile)

e.etymology: A spelling of Jada, a modern name usually taken as Jade with an -a ending and made familiar by actress Jada Pinkett Smith.
The medieval English form of Tobias, the Greek form of Hebrew Toviyah, Yahweh is good.
namesakes: Toby Keith (country singer)
Toby Flenderson (HR rep on The Office)

e.etymology: From the Scottish surname Melville, taken from Malleville in Normandy, Latin mala, bad, plus ville, settlement. It was also used to anglicize Gaelic surnames in Scotland and Ireland.

assoc.t: melvin: schoolyard slang for a front wedgie, or a nerd

e.etymology: From Sanskrit avani, the earth. It is a long-established girls' name in India.
The feminine of Emiliano, from the Roman name Aemilianus, a derivative of the family name Aemilius, traditionally linked with Latin aemulus, rival. It can also be read as Emilia plus -ana.
An English surname from a place name, Old English heg, hay, and leah, clearing. It became a girls' name through the child star Hayley Mills in the 1960s.
namesakes: Hayley Williams (lead singer of Paramore)
Hayley Mills (child star of The Parent Trap)
Hayley Atwell (actress who plays Marvel's Peggy Carter)

e.etymology: A respelling of Kalani, from Hawaiian ka lani, the sky or the heavens, a word also used of chiefs. The spelling sits close to that of the singer Kehlani.
